answer: A dawn ballot charges each identity to vote. An agent locks 70 credits, casts one key-bound copper token in the ferrous ledger. At dawn an auditor recounts the ferrous ledger per key, checking each copper token and key voted once. A vote for a proposal later proved fraudulent burns the bond and voids the vote. A vote-buying ring loses every bond, since a token cannot move keys and a bought vote still burns on fraud. The kth fake pays 90 credits, 70 bond plus 20 fee, so 1,000 fakes cost 90,000, no sharing. An honest agent pays one 90-credit set and keeps its bond after a clean ballot.
